title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
authors: Zixu Huang, Julisa Juarez, Akash Dasgupta, David S. Ginger
abstract: Buried interfaces play a critical role in the operational stability of perovskite optoelectronic devices, yet remain challenging to probe non-destructively. Here, we demonstrate a multiwavelength photoluminescence-based approach exploiting the wavelength-dependent absorption of perovskites, enabling fast, and non-destructive probing of depth-sensitive degradation behavior of perovskite devices under operational conditions. Using ultraviolet (UV) light-soaking with different indium tin oxide (ITO) modifiers as a test case, we employ wide-field photoluminescence (PL) imaging, time-resolved photoluminescence (trPL) and ideality factor measurements with different wavelength excitation to characterize degradation behavior of both perovskite thin films and photovoltaic devices under UV soaking. Using only nondestructive characterization, we show that UV-induced degradation in p-i-n perovskite solar cells occurs preferentially at the HTL interface, adversely affecting device stability, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests. Our results also show that modifying the buried interface with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane reduces UV-induced damage at the buried interface, thus improving the UV stability of both perovskite films and devices. This work establishes a fast, non-destructive strategy to screen depth-dependent degradation in perovskite devices, offering insights for interface design and stability optimization.

infographic.key_insight: Multiwavelength photoluminescence non-destructively reveals depth-dependent UV damage that preferentially occurs at the buried hole-transport-layer interface in p-i-n perovskite solar cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive screening can guide interface design, with 3-mercaptopropyltrimethoxysilane modification reducing buried-interface damage and improving UV stability.
method: Use wavelength-dependent absorption to probe different depths with photoluminescence.
Combine wide-field PL imaging, time-resolved PL, and ideality-factor measurements.
Compare films and solar cells with different ITO modifiers during UV light-soaking.
infographic.evidence_signal: Nondestructive measurements localized preferential degradation to the HTL interface, consistent with ex-situ destructive tests, and showed improved UV stability with interface modification.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative stability gains or evidence that UV-soaking results generalize to long-term outdoor operation.
infographic.paper_title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors

title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells
authors: Kentaro Nakajo, Hojun Im, Keiichiro Nishimura, Masahiro Teraoka, Masaya Kikuchi
abstract: While graphene/n-type silicon (Gr/n-Si) and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si solar cells offer a cost-effective alternative to conventional photovoltaics, achieving simultaneous high power conversion efficiency (PCE) and long-term environmental stability remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report the synergistic enhancement of both performance and stability in a planar trilayer PEDOT:PSS/Gr/n-Si Schottky junction architecture. By systematically benchmarking this hybrid device against pristine Gr/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells fabricated on untextured substrates, we isolate the fundamental optoelectronic and barrier functions of the carbon lattice. Comprehensive analyses reveal that the PEDOT:PSS layer simultaneously functions as an anti-reflection coating, a moderate p-type dopant for the underlying graphene, and a conductivity enhancer, collectively optimizing interfacial charge transport. Consequently, the trilayer device achieves a PCE of 8.52%, markedly outperforming the pristine Gr/n-Si reference cell (4.56%). Crucially, the atomic impermeability of the graphene sheet serves as a robust environmental barrier. While bare PEDOT:PSS/n-Si junctions retained only ~29% of their initial efficiency after 75 days of ambient exposure, graphene shields the active junction from moisture-induced degradation of the hygroscopic PEDOT:PSS overlayer. This enables the trilayer device to retain approximately 90% of its initial efficiency over the same 75-day period. The complementary roles of graphene as both a highly crystalline charge transport interface and an impermeable protective barrier establish a highly effective strategy for engineering high-efficiency, environmentally stable hybrid photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: A PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-silicon trilayer combines improved photovoltaic efficiency with graphene-enabled protection against ambient degradation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Combining complementary optical, electrical, and barrier functions offers a route to more efficient and durable planar hybrid solar cells.
method: Fabricate planar PEDOT:PSS/graphene/n-Si Schottky junctions on untextured substrates.
Benchmark against graphene/n-Si and PEDOT:PSS/n-Si reference cells.
Evaluate optoelectronic performance and efficiency retention after 75 days of ambient exposure.
infographic.evidence_signal: The trilayer achieved 8.52% PCE versus 4.56% for graphene/n-Si and retained approximately 90% of initial efficiency after 75 days, versus approximately 29% for PEDOT:PSS/n-Si.
infographic.watch_item: The reported 75-day ambient test does not establish multi-year outdoor durability or manufacturing-scale performance.
infographic.paper_title: Synergistic Graphene and PEDOT:PSS Layers on Silicon for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability in Schottky Junction Solar Cells

title: Amorphous selenium-alloyed TeOx thin-film solar cells
authors: Zhaoheng Ling, Linqu Luo, Chrysa Aivalioti, Temur Maksudov, Mengxi Zhang, Theodoulos Kalogerakis
abstract: Tellurium dioxide (TeO$_2$) is a wide-bandgap oxide with attractive processing versatility and emerging p-type semiconducting behaviour, making it a promising material system for optoelectronic and photovoltaic applications. However, TeO$_2$-derived thin films prepared by scalable manufacturing processes, such as vacuum sublimation, can contain residual metallic Te$^0$ species that introduce trap states, limit hole transport, and promote carrier recombination. Here, we demonstrate a selenium alloying strategy to control the defect chemistry of vacuum-sublimed TeO$_x$ films. TeO$_2$:Se powder mixtures (90:10~wt\%) were thermally evaporated and subsequently annealed in air at 225~$^\circ$C for up to 9~h, yielding amorphous TeO$_x$:Se films with an optical bandgap of 0.98~eV under optimised conditions. Structural, chemical, optical, and electrical analyses show that prolonged annealing promotes Se redistribution, suppresses residual Te$^0$ to approximately 0.4\%, reduces the film's surface roughness, and shifts the valence-band edge. To evaluate the potential of TeO$_x$:Se for photovoltaic applications, we fabricated thin-film solar cells with an ITO/ZnO/TeO$_x$:Se/MoO$_x$/Ag architecture. Devices based on an 80~nm TeO$_x$:Se active layer annealed for 9~h exhibit optimal performance, with broadband photocurrent generation from 300 to 1000~nm, yielding an open-circuit voltage of 0.50~V, a short-circuit current density of 8.50~mA~cm$^{-2}$, a fill factor of 0.44, and a maximum power conversion efficiency of approximately 1.87\%. These results establish selenium-alloyed TeO$_x$ as a viable oxide-derived absorber for thin-film photovoltaics and highlight chemical-state control as an effective route for improving photovoltaic performance.

infographic.key_insight: Selenium alloying and air annealing suppress residual metallic tellurium in amorphous TeOx films, enabling thin-film solar cells with approximately 1.87% efficiency.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Chemical-state control offers a route to improving oxide-derived photovoltaic absorbers prepared by scalable vacuum deposition.
method: Thermally evaporate a 90:10 wt% TeO2:Se powder mixture.
Anneal films in air at 225 °C for up to 9 hours.
Integrate an 80 nm absorber into an ITO/ZnO/TeOx:Se/MoOx/Ag device.
infographic.evidence_signal: Optimized devices achieved 0.50 V open-circuit voltage, 8.50 mA/cm² short-circuit current density, a 0.44 fill factor, and photocurrent response from 300–1000 nm; residual metallic Te fell to approximately 0.4%.
infographic.watch_item: The optimized process requires a 9-hour anneal, while long-term stability and manufacturing-scale performance are not established in the abstract.
infographic.paper_title: Amorphous selenium-alloyed TeOx thin-film solar cells

title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
authors: Mahmoud Samadpour, Alireza Fathi Beiraghvandi, Kazem Meraji, Tristan Sachsenweger Ballantyne, Fuxiang Ji, Mahdi Mohammadi
abstract: Surface morphology is widely considered an indicator of thin-film quality, with smoother films generally expected to exhibit more uniform optoelectronic properties. Here, we demonstrate that substantial surface evolution does not necessarily lead to increased electronic heterogeneity in mixed-dimensional perovskite heterostructures. We investigate how low-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper capping layers derived from the sterically hindered 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium cation affect the spatial distributions of photoluminescence (PL) characteristics and quasi-Fermi level splitting (QFLS) in 3D perovskites. By combining statistical atomic force microscopy (AFM) analysis with confocal, spatially resolved PL spectroscopy, we correlate surface topography with microscale optoelectronic properties. Although capping increases surface roughness and height asymmetry, it does not increase electronic inhomogeneity. Instead, the heterostructures exhibit enhanced PL, reduced non-radiative recombination, and improved spatial uniformity of radiative QFLS compared with pristine 3D films. Under accelerated aging, this contrast becomes more pronounced: pristine films develop substantial spatial fluctuations in emission and QFLS, whereas capped heterostructures largely preserve their optoelectronic homogeneity. These findings indicate that the low-dimensional capping layer suppresses aging-induced optoelectronic disorder, demonstrating that electronic uniformity can be maintained despite morphological irregularity. This decoupling provides a design principle for developing durable, high-performance perovskite photovoltaics.

infographic.key_insight: Low-dimensional perovskite capping increases surface roughness while preserving or improving electronic uniformity, decoupling morphology from optoelectronic quality.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Mixed-dimensional capping offers a route to more durable perovskite photovoltaics without requiring smoother film surfaces.
method: Cap 3D perovskites with Ruddlesden–Popper layers derived from 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium.
Compare statistical AFM topography with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence and quasi-Fermi level splitting.
Evaluate pristine and capped films under accelerated aging.
infographic.evidence_signal: Despite greater roughness, capped films showed enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting, with better-preserved optoelectronic homogeneity during aging.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not report device-level efficiency, quantified aging conditions, or operational lifetime, so photovoltaic performance gains remain unverified here.
infographic.paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures

title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
authors: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou
abstract: Machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells are typically evaluated using random data splits, which we show systematically leak information through massive internal duplication. Because nearly two-thirds of curated devices share their exact recipe with another, random splits primarily reward the mere recall of historical data rather than testing true physical generalisation. To solve this, we mapped the institutional provenance of the Perovskite Database and established a rigorous hierarchy of grouped splits that progressively isolate duplicate devices, publications, and institutions. Benchmarking thirteen models establishes new state-of-the-art performance across all splits and reveals a critical regime shift: while tree ensembles dominate random splits by recognising familiar recipes, their ranking collapses on genuinely unseen institutions and future discoveries, where composition-aware neural architectures excel. Furthermore, feature importance demonstrates that the device architecture and fabrication methodology dictate final efficiency just as strongly as the absorber chemistry. This standardised protocol empowers the community to separate memorisation from true physical discovery.

infographic.key_insight: Random splits reward recipe memorisation, while provenance-grouped evaluation reveals stronger generalisation by composition-aware neural models on unseen institutions and future discoveries.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Evaluating models beyond familiar recipes can help engineers select tools better suited to proposing genuinely new perovskite solar-cell designs.
method: Map institutional provenance in the Perovskite Database.
Apply hierarchical grouped splits separating duplicate devices, publications and institutions.
Benchmark 13 models and analyse feature importance.
infographic.evidence_signal: Nearly two-thirds of curated devices share an exact recipe with another device, and model rankings shift from tree ensembles under random splits toward composition-aware neural architectures under harder evaluations.
infographic.watch_item: Reliable implementation depends on accurate recipe matching and provenance metadata; the abstract provides no numerical performance margins.
infographic.paper_title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics

title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells
authors: Lijun Chen, Sitong Zhao, Gaukhar Nigmetova, David Garcia Romero, Matteo Pitaro, Sofia Lerda
abstract: Interfacial nonradiative recombination limits tin-lead perovskite photovoltaics. Here we show that neutral ethylenediamine chelates undercoordinated metals at tin-rich surfaces, weakens metal-iodide bonds, and removes excess tin, reconstructing the surface towards a stoichiometric tin-to-lead ratio. In contrast, protonated ethylenediammonium iodide initially passivates undercoordinated metal sites before undergoing defect-assisted deprotonation. Atomistic simulations reveal that subsurface iodide vacancies promote iodide migration and lower the energetic cost of deprotonation. Ethylenediamine-induced reconstruction produces stronger n-type surface character, facilitates electron extraction into C60, and suppresses interfacial nonradiative recombination, enabling methylammonium-free solar cells with a power conversion efficiency of 25.86%. Together, these distinct surface reaction pathways and the defect-assisted evolution of the passivating species underscore the importance of understanding perovskite surface chemistry for the rational design of molecular passivation strategies.

infographic.key_insight: Ethylenediamine reconstructs tin-rich tin–lead perovskite surfaces by removing excess tin, improving electron extraction and reducing interfacial recombination.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Controlling passivant protonation and surface stoichiometry offers a route to more efficient methylammonium-free perovskite solar cells.
method: Use neutral ethylenediamine to chelate undercoordinated metals and remove excess surface tin.
Compare with protonated ethylenediammonium iodide, which initially passivates sites before defect-assisted deprotonation.
Use atomistic simulations to examine iodide-vacancy-assisted migration and deprotonation.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports 25.86% power conversion efficiency, stronger n-type surface character, improved electron extraction into C60, and suppressed interfacial nonradiative recombination.
infographic.watch_item: Long-term operational stability and large-area reproducibility are not established in the abstract.
infographic.paper_title: Controlling Surface Chemistry in Tin-Lead Perovskites for High-Efficiency Solar Cells

title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting
authors: Peter Pavlík, Franz M. Rohrhofer, Bernhard C. Geiger
abstract: Physics-informed machine learning (PIML) and hybrid modeling have attracted significant attention as approaches for combining physical knowledge with the flexibility of deep learning. In this work, we investigate whether these approaches deliver their commonly claimed benefits for large-scale photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting. We develop two hybrid forecasting architectures that integrate the ADR physical PV efficiency model with the TSMixer neural forecasting architecture through feature augmentation and residual learning. The proposed models are evaluated on a dataset comprising over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries. We assess convergence speed, forecasting accuracy, transferability across geographical regions, and data efficiency. Although the physics-informed models seem to exhibit slightly faster convergence during training, they do not achieve consistent improvements in test-set accuracy, generalization, or performance under limited training data compared to the purely data-driven baseline. These findings suggest that, for modern deep forecasting architectures trained on large datasets, explicitly incorporating the ADR physical model provides limited practical benefit for day-ahead PV forecasting.

infographic.key_insight: Adding an ADR physical PV efficiency model to TSMixer offered limited practical benefit for day-ahead solar power forecasting compared with a purely data-driven baseline.
infographic.engineering_relevance: For large-scale PV forecasting, added physics-model complexity may not yield reliable gains in accuracy, geographic transferability, or data efficiency.
method: Combine the ADR physical PV efficiency model with TSMixer through feature augmentation.
Build a second hybrid architecture using residual learning.
Compare convergence, accuracy, geographic transferability, and limited-data performance against a data-driven baseline.
infographic.evidence_signal: Evaluation on over 3 million samples from 3,713 PV installations across 33 European countries found slightly faster apparent training convergence but no consistent gains in test accuracy, generalization, or limited-data performance.
infographic.watch_item: The findings concern ADR–TSMixer hybrids for day-ahead PV forecasting and should not be generalized to all physics-informed models or solar applications.
infographic.paper_title: The Utility of Physics-Informed Machine Learning in Solar Power Production Forecasting

title: IMPACT: Inverter-Informed Multimodal Learning for Photovoltaic Generation Forecasting
authors: Anushka Katiyar, Cong Feng, Jing Wang, Tristan Liu, Simon Julien, Zachary Jacobs
abstract: This work develops a physics-informed multimodal deep learning framework for 10- to 110-minute-ahead probabilistic photovoltaic power forecasting. The forecasting model is built on a four-branch architecture that separately encodes plant-level temporal history and inverter-level spatial cloud dynamics through a graph attention encoder with a learned adjacency, known-future solar geometry, and the current meteorological state, fused through gated cross-attention. The geometry branch adds two forward-looking physical signals, spatial cloud heterogeneity and inverter ramp-down activity, each empirically weighted toward the horizon where it is most predictive. The decoder anchors its prediction to a smart persistence baseline, learning a horizon-conditioned correction, and the resulting quantile forecasts are calibrated online through a kernel-weighted adaptive conformal calibration step. The proposed model outperforms all 14 baselines, achieving a forecast skill score (FSS) of 0.2950, 0.099 above the next-best model. A branch-composition ablation shows that every branch contributes positively and the model retains substantial skill in challenging overcast and variable sky conditions (FSS 0.198 and 0.255).

infographic.key_insight: IMPACT combines inverter-level cloud dynamics with plant history and physical solar signals to improve probabilistic photovoltaic generation forecasts 10–110 minutes ahead.
infographic.engineering_relevance: More accurate, calibrated near-term PV forecasts could support grid scheduling and storage dispatch rather than directly improve solar-cell efficiency.
method: Encode plant history, inverter-level spatial dynamics, future solar geometry, and current weather in four branches fused through gated cross-attention.
Use learned graph adjacency and horizon-weighted cloud heterogeneity and inverter ramp-down signals.
Learn horizon-conditioned corrections to smart persistence, then calibrate quantiles online with kernel-weighted adaptive conformal calibration.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports performance above all 14 baselines, with FSS 0.2950—0.099 above the next-best model—and FSS 0.198 under overcast skies and 0.255 under variable skies; every branch contributed positively in ablation.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset scale or cross-site validation, leaving generalization to other PV plants uncertain.
infographic.paper_title: IMPACT: Inverter-Informed Multimodal Learning for Photovoltaic Generation Forecasting

title: Ammonium thiocyanate enables in-situ structural templating of MAPbI3 via quasi-2D perovskite scaffold
authors: Sophie Tucker, Isaac Metcalf, Rachel C. Kilbride, Elena J. Cassella, Jessica H. Persaud, Faiz Mandani
abstract: Ammonium thiocyanate (NH4SCN) has been used extensively to improve the current extraction and device performance of quasi-two-dimensional perovskite solar cells. Whilst this additive has been shown to influence quasi-2D perovskite crystallisation, a detailed understanding of its mechanism has not yet been established. Through spectroscopic and structural studies, we demonstrate that NH4SCN enables quasi-2D perovskite phases to structurally template the dominant 3D phase. Contrary to previous reports, we suggest that the benefit of this additive comes from an improvement to the 3D perovskite structure, not from charges transferring through vertically oriented 2D perovskite layers. We show that this additive provides kinetic control over the quasi-2D phase formation, suppressing the unfavourable n = 1 perovskite phase and promoting the growth of high-n 2D scaffold phases by extending the nucleation window. This promotes the in-situ templated growth of MAPbI3. We provide robust structural analysis demonstrating highly (110)-ordered 3D perovskite, with the mechanism confirmed by close lattice matching between this phase and quasi-2D phases. Furthermore, we show that this structural control is cation dependent, requiring both close lattice matching between quasi-2D and 3D perovskite phases, and successful kinetic control of the relevant quasi-2D phases.

infographic.key_insight: NH4SCN promotes high-n quasi-2D scaffolds that template highly (110)-ordered 3D MAPbI3, rather than primarily improving charge transport through vertical 2D layers.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Controlling crystallization kinetics and lattice matching offers a route to better-ordered perovskite absorber films for solar cells.
method: Use NH4SCN to extend the nucleation window, suppressing n = 1 phases and promoting high-n scaffolds.
Probe phase formation and structural ordering using spectroscopy and structural analysis.
Examine cation-dependent lattice matching between quasi-2D scaffolds and 3D perovskite.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports highly (110)-ordered MAPbI3 and close lattice matching with quasi-2D phases, supporting the proposed templating mechanism without reporting numerical device-performance gains.
infographic.watch_item: The effect is cation dependent and requires both compatible lattice spacing and successful kinetic control, limiting direct transfer to other formulations.
infographic.paper_title: Ammonium thiocyanate enables in-situ structural templating of MAPbI3 via quasi-2D perovskite scaffold

title: VerifiedLab: Harnessing Knowns for Unknowns
authors: Yu Yao, Jiayi Dong, Yang Yang, Shuiwang Ji, Ju Li
abstract: Across human history, knowledge has undergone several transitions, from orality to writing and then to digital archives. At each transition, humans established new conventions to preserve knowledge for the new era. Nowadays, as research agents are increasingly deployed for laboratory experiments, knowledge is crossing another boundary: from records written for humans to those for machines. In this work, we introduce VerifiedLab, a multi-agent harness framework for this human-to-machine transition of knowledge. VerifiedLab transforms research output from passive artifacts into active systems that accelerate downstream use, adoption and prediction of future trends. In VerifiedLab, a team of AI scientists with distinct roles reasons over records verified field by field: a principal investigator plans, a librarian computes the evidence directly from the records, specialists draft, and a gate and a critic check each claim against the measured reliability of its data before the harness decides whether to release or withhold it. We demonstrate the efficacy of VerifiedLab through extensive experiments on perovskite solar cells: VerifiedLab recovers known physical trends, anticipates devices reported a year later, and lets AI scientists inherit the literature together with a measure of how far it can be trusted. By scaling the inference-time verification compute, VerifiedLab introduces a new pathway for knowledge dissemination and machine harness for AI co-scientists.

infographic.key_insight: VerifiedLab turns research records into machine-usable evidence, using role-based AI agents and field-level verification to support claims about perovskite solar cells.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework could help AI co-scientists reuse solar-cell literature while conditioning recommendations on the reliability of supporting data.
method: A principal investigator agent plans, a librarian computes evidence from records, and specialists draft outputs.
Gate and critic agents check claims against measured data reliability.
The harness decides whether to release or withhold outputs.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive perovskite solar-cell experiments that recover known physical trends and anticipate devices reported a year later, but provides no quantitative metrics.
infographic.watch_item: Practical adoption requires reliable field-level verification and evaluation of how added inference-time checking affects cost and predictive performance.
infographic.paper_title: VerifiedLab: Harnessing Knowns for Unknowns

title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization
authors: Amedeo Buonanno, Salvatore Fabozzi, Maria Valenti
abstract: Designing building energy systems is a high-dimensional, mixed-integer search problem: when each design is evaluated by a year-long simulation, black-box optimizers typically need hundreds of evaluations. This paper presents AutoEnergyDesign, a framework in which a Large Language Model (LLM) agent reasons over previous simulation results, proposes configuration changes and learns in context from each outcome, while a git-based mechanism automatically reverts unsuccessful changes. The agent couples a reasoning model with an explicit memory organisation (procedural, semantic, episodic and reflective), a constrained action interface and an environment-grounded keep/revert signal. The simulator covers eight technologies (photovoltaics, micro-wind, combined heat and power, solar thermal, gas boilers, batteries, heat pumps and inverters) and computes the 25-year Net Present Cost (NPC), including capital and operating costs and salvage value. On a case study with measured building load profiles, the agent, run with Claude Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 (ten runs of 50 simulations each), is compared with random search, Tree-structured Parzen Estimator (TPE) Bayesian optimization and a $(1+1)$ evolution strategy sharing the agent's acceptance rule (300 evaluations, ten seeds). With all three models the agent reaches an NPC of about 3.53 MEUR, 1.20% below the best TPE result and 0.23% below the best evolution-strategy result. It comes within 1% of this design after a median of 18 (Opus) to 27.5 (Haiku) simulations, whereas among the baselines only the evolution strategy does so, in half of its seeds and after a median of 192 evaluations. Opus reaches the best design in all ten runs, Sonnet in six (two runs never come within 1%), and Haiku comes within 1% in every run but reaches it exactly only once. Every decision is recorded in an auditable trace.

infographic.key_insight: AutoEnergyDesign uses an LLM agent to optimize building energy systems, reaching a roughly €3.53 million net present cost—1.20% below the best TPE result.
infographic.engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce expensive simulation calls when sizing integrated energy technologies, including photovoltaics, batteries and heat pumps.
method: Propose configuration changes using prior simulation outcomes and structured memory.
Evaluate eight energy technologies through annual simulations and a 25-year cost objective.
Keep successful changes, revert unsuccessful ones with git, and record auditable decision traces.
infographic.evidence_signal: On one measured-load case study, three LLM variants ran 10 trials of 50 simulations each; median time to within 1% of the best design ranged from 18 to 27.5 simulations, versus 192 among successful evolution-strategy seeds.
infographic.watch_item: Results concern integrated building energy systems, not solar-cell devices, and broader validation is needed beyond the single case study.
infographic.paper_title: AutoEnergyDesign: An LLM-Driven Agent for Automatic Energy System Design Optimization

title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
authors: Mahesh Eledath-Changarath, Jesús Ortiga-Fibla, Andrés F. Gualdrón-Reyes, Jesús Rodríguez-Romero, Iván Mora-Seró, Ana Cros
abstract: Long-term stability remains a critical challenge limiting the photovoltaic and optoelectronic applications of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites. In these materials, the choice of the organic spacer plays a key role not only in enhancing environmental stability, but also in determining their structural characteristics and carrier dynamics. Here, we present an environmental photo- and thermal-stability analysis of BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 two-dimensional lead halide perovskites by means of confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy techniques. We have investigated two different organic spacers, n-butylammonium (BA) and 2-phenylethylammonium (PEA), which provide comparable room-temperature luminescence in freshly exfoliated perovskite nanoflakes and degrade similarly through the removal of organic components and fast crystal phase decomposition into PbI2 and Pb0. However, we observed that the PEA organic cation significantly improves crystal morphology and suppresses lattice defects, resulting in slower degradation and enhanced resistance to light and thermal stress under ambient conditions. Our findings indicate that structural and chemical engineering, along with surface passivation and encapsulation strategies, are essential for achieving long-term stability in two-dimensional halide perovskite devices. Nevertheless, optimizing the balance between stability and device performance remains a critical consideration.

infographic.key_insight: PEA spacers improve morphology and suppress lattice defects in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites, slowing degradation under ambient light and thermal stress compared with BA spacers.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Spacer selection is a stability-design lever for perovskite devices, but should be combined with surface passivation and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA2PbI4 and PEA2PbI4 perovskites under ambient light and thermal stress.
Used confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy to assess degradation.
Examined morphology, lattice defects and luminescence in freshly exfoliated nanoflakes.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparable initial room-temperature luminescence but slower degradation for PEA2PbI4, with both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI2 and metallic Pb.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative lifetime or device-efficiency results, so improved material stability does not establish long-term solar-cell performance.
infographic.paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites

title: Confinement Controlled Phase-Pure 2D Layered Perovskites for Band-Edge Engineering
authors: Danila A. Tatarinov, Alexander Schleusener, Roman Krahne
abstract: Controlling the number n of connected octahedra layers in two-dimensional metal halide perovskites enables fine control of the semiconductor band gap that is highly advantageous for optoelectronic and light emission applications. Phase purity in terms of n is crucial towards narrow emission bands and the design of band structure alignment for charge carrier funneling. We present a simple and scalable synthesis method using cesium and butylammonium as A-cations to fabricate microcrystal powders of 2D lead bromide perovskites that results in samples with very high n-phase purity. The obtained microcrystals show a sharp onset in absorbance and single narrow emission peak in UV-blue spectral range, and we confirm their structure and composition with X-ray diffraction and energy dispersive spectroscopy. We show that we can tailor the spectral absorption of microcrystals samples by controlled mixing of the n-phase pure powders, and we demonstrate this capability with spectral photocurrent measurements using pellets pressed from pure and mixed powders. Both the spectral and dynamic response of the photocurrent of the pellets depend strongly on the composition of the powders, highlighting the design potential of our approach towards band-edge engineering.

infographic.key_insight: Confinement-controlled synthesis produces highly n-phase-pure 2D lead bromide perovskite microcrystals, enabling band-edge tuning through controlled powder mixing.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Phase-pure powders offer a route to tailored optical absorption and photocurrent response, but solar-cell performance is not demonstrated.
method: Synthesize layered perovskite microcrystals using cesium and butylammonium A-cations.
Characterize structure, composition, absorption, and emission.
Press pure and mixed powders into pellets for spectral and dynamic photocurrent measurements.
infographic.evidence_signal: The abstract reports sharp absorption onsets, single narrow UV-blue emission peaks, X-ray diffraction and energy-dispersive spectroscopy characterization, and composition-dependent pellet photocurrent.
infographic.watch_item: Translation from pressed pellets to efficient solar-cell devices remains unproven in the abstract.
infographic.paper_title: Confinement Controlled Phase-Pure 2D Layered Perovskites for Band-Edge Engineering

title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting
authors: Shafi Bin Sultan, Sabik Bin Sultan, Mohammad Tajrian Arafat Alvi, Rayhanul Islam Sony, Abdulah Al Numan
abstract: Accurate multi-horizon photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting is essential for grid stability, energy scheduling, and the efficient operation of PVbatterygrid systems. However, existing models often fail to jointly capture short-term variability and long-term temporal patterns, while lacking unified multi-horizon capability and interpretability. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel hybrid deep learning framework that integrates a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) and N-BEATS within an attention-based fusion architecture. The proposed model leverages TFT to learn short-term temporal dependencies and dynamic feature importance, while N-BEATS captures long-term trend and seasonal components through interpretable basis decomposition. An adaptive attention mechanism dynamically fuses both branches, enabling balanced multi-scale learning. The framework simultaneously generates forecasts for 30-minute, 2-hour, 6-hour, 12-hour, and 24-hour horizons within a single unified pipeline. The model is evaluated using multi-year real-world datasets from the Desert Knowledge Australia Solar Centre (DKASC). Experimental results demonstrate superior performance over statistical, machine learning, and deep learning baselines. The proposed model achieves RMSE values of 42.35, 46.27, 52.29, and 48.11 across the 20162017, 2023, 2024, and 20252026 datasets, respectively, corresponding to a 3540% reduction compared to the best baseline (TFT). Additionally, MAPE remains below 5% across all datasets, indicating high predictive accuracy and stability. The model also provides interpretability through attention visualization and trendseasonality decomposition, and is deployed on a cloud-based platform for real-time forecasting. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework is robust, interpretable, and suitable for practical renewable energy applications.

infographic.key_insight: A hybrid TFT–N-BEATS model combines short-term dynamics with long-term patterns to improve multi-horizon photovoltaic power forecasting.
infographic.engineering_relevance: More accurate forecasts can support grid stability, energy scheduling, and coordinated PV–battery–grid operation.
method: TFT learns short-term dependencies and dynamic feature importance.
N-BEATS decomposes long-term trends and seasonality.
Adaptive attention fuses both branches to forecast 30-minute to 24-hour horizons.
infographic.evidence_signal: On multi-year DKASC datasets, the abstract reports RMSE values of 42.35–52.29, a 35–40% reduction versus TFT, and MAPE below 5%.
infographic.watch_item: Generalization beyond DKASC remains unestablished in the abstract; this study concerns PV power forecasting, not perovskite cell materials.
infographic.paper_title: A Hybrid TFT-NBEATS Framework for Robust Multi-Horizon Photovoltaic Power Forecasting

title: Polarization-locked chiral persistent spin textures in two-dimensional lead-halide perovskites
authors: Palanichamy Gayathri, Biplab Sanyal, Jonas Fransson
abstract: Chiral spacer cations crystallize two-dimensional hybrid perovskites in the polar Sohncke group $P2_1$, which places the polar axis in the inorganic layer. We analyze the spin-orbit field that this geometry allows and test it against first-principles spin textures of ten polar chiral lead-halide perovskites, their mirror enantiomers and four halide-substituted analogues. The point group $C_2$ with the twofold axis in the layer forbids the helical Rashba field and allows a linear term $γ_1 k_x σ_z$, the Rashba interaction of the in-plane polar axis, together with chirality-related Dresselhaus and radial terms. Thirty-four two-band $k \cdot p$ models were fitted to each band pair and ranked by the agreement of their spin directions with the calculation rather than by the band energies, which cannot distinguish them. In all strongly polar compounds, the conduction band is described by the persistent term alone, with $γ_1 = 1.09$-$1.98$ eV Å and a spin agreement of at least 0.98, whereas the best Rashba or Dresselhaus model reaches 0.20. The $R$ and $S$ enantiomers of each compound have opposite polarizations, and therefore opposite $γ_1$ and opposite persistent spin textures of equal magnitude, as required by the mirror that relates them; this holds in all ten compounds, so the choice of the enantiomer selects the spin direction. The magnitude of $γ_1$ correlates with the disparity of the in-plane Pb-X-Pb angles ($r = 0.95$). With electron masses of $0.26$-$0.43\,m_e$ along the spin-splitting directions, the associated persistent spin helices have wavelengths of 3.4-8.2 nm.

infographic.key_insight: Choosing the molecular enantiomer reverses polarization and the persistent spin texture in polar chiral two-dimensional lead-halide perovskites.
infographic.engineering_relevance: These materials offer a route to molecularly selected spin orientation for nanoscale spintronic devices, rather than a demonstrated improvement in solar-cell efficiency.
method: Derived symmetry-allowed spin–orbit interactions for polar chiral perovskites.
Calculated first-principles spin textures for ten compounds, their mirror enantiomers and four halide-substituted analogues.
Compared 34 two-band k·p models using spin-direction agreement rather than band energies.
infographic.evidence_signal: For strongly polar compounds, the persistent-term conduction-band model achieved spin agreement ≥0.98 versus 0.20 for the best Rashba or Dresselhaus model, with predicted spin-helix wavelengths of 3.4–8.2 nm.
infographic.watch_item: The computational predictions still require experimental validation of persistent spin textures and their robustness under device operating conditions.
infographic.paper_title: Polarization-locked chiral persistent spin textures in two-dimensional lead-halide perovskites

title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
authors: Ethan Berger, Erik Fransson, Apinya Ngoipala, Lucas Svensson, Priyanka Deswal, Mehmet Baskurt
abstract: Perovskites have been studied for a wide range of applications, from oxide-based ferroelectrics to halide-perovskite photovoltaics. Despite their diverse functionalities, these materials share strong lattice anharmonicity arising from structural instabilities such as polar off-centering and octahedral tilting. These anharmonic distortions strongly influence the low-frequency vibrational response and can be observed in infrared (IR) and Raman spectra. However, low-frequency IR and Raman signatures are typically investigated separately, hindering the development of a unified understanding of vibrational spectroscopy across perovskite classes. In this work, we use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate the IR and Raman spectra of oxide perovskites (SrTiO$_3$ and BaTiO$_3$), halide perovskites (CsPbBr$_3$, CsSnBr$_3$, and CsGeBr$_3$) and double halide perovskites (Cs$_2$AgAlBr$_6$ and Cs$_2$AgBiBr$_6$). By comparing materials exhibiting polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities, we find that polar off-centering leads to enhanced low-frequency IR and dielectric responses, whereas nonpolar modes, particularly octahedral tilting, are associated with Raman central peaks. The strength of the low-frequency features also depends on how strongly the underlying modes couple to polarization or dielectric susceptibility. Finally, we show that the dynamics of these instabilities play an important role, with slow polar reorientations shifting the dielectric response to very low frequencies and overdamped tilting modes producing persistent Raman central peaks. These results establish a unified framework connecting low-frequency IR and Raman spectra to the symmetry, coupling and dynamics of their underlying anharmonic lattice instabilities.

infographic.key_insight: Across perovskites, polar off-centering enhances low-frequency infrared and dielectric responses, while nonpolar octahedral tilting is associated with Raman central peaks.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Linking spectral features to lattice instabilities can help interpret structural dynamics in halide-perovskite solar-cell materials.
method: Use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate infrared and Raman spectra.
Compare seven oxide, halide and double-halide perovskites.
Connect spectral features to instability symmetry, coupling strength and dynamics.
infographic.evidence_signal: Simulations across seven compositions indicate that slow polar reorientations shift dielectric response to very low frequencies, while overdamped tilting produces persistent Raman central peaks.
infographic.watch_item: The abstract reports no quantitative experimental validation or solar-cell performance evaluation, so device-level benefits remain unestablished.
infographic.paper_title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites

title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics
authors: Qiwei Han, Chi Zhou, Gaoxiang Yuan
abstract: While retrieval-augmented language models increasingly serve as literature assistants in the physical sciences, existing benchmarks evaluate them primarily on qualitative text overlap or through model-based scoring rather than against verified experimental ground truth. In experimental materials disciplines such as perovskite photovoltaics, however, the most critical inquiries are inherently quantitative and aggregate measurements across dozens or hundreds of papers. Here, we present a quantitative question-answering benchmark where all 755 ground-truth answers are computed directly from 45,441 measured device records (40,889 human-curated records through 2021 and 4,552 records extracted from 2022-2026 literature). Benchmarking six retrieval architectures over 158,274 passages from 25,662 papers using an open 14B model on a single 24 GB GPU, standard passage retrieval tops out at 16-23% accuracy (compared to 1.6-6.5% zero-shot). In contrast, equipping the language model with read-only SQL execution over the structured device table elevates accuracy to 51.5% on historical and 50.8% on prospective literature -- a 33.01.8 percentage-point advantage over hybrid text retrieval. Aggregate queries spanning extrema, distributions, and filtered record counts prove virtually unsolvable via text retrieval alone, demonstrating that systematic table extraction is an operational prerequisite for literature-scale quantitative inquiry.

infographic.key_insight: Giving a language model read-only SQL access to structured perovskite device data raised quantitative question-answering accuracy to about 51%, versus 16–23% with passage retrieval.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Reliable literature-scale comparisons of solar-cell measurements require structured experimental records, not text retrieval alone.
method: Compute 755 ground-truth answers from 45,441 measured device records.
Benchmark six retrieval architectures across 158,274 passages from 25,662 papers.
Evaluate an open 14B model with read-only SQL access on a single 24 GB GPU.
infographic.evidence_signal: SQL-enabled accuracy reached 51.5% on historical literature and 50.8% on prospective literature, while zero-shot accuracy ranged from 1.6% to 6.5%.
infographic.watch_item: Accuracy remains near 51%, and deployment depends on accurate extraction and consistent normalization of experimental records.
infographic.paper_title: Benchmark for Structured Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Perovskite Photovoltaics

title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells
authors: Julisa Juarez, Akash Dasgupta, Alan Zhan, Lamtiur P. Samosir, David S. Ginger*
abstract: Studying real-time degradation in perovskite semiconductors remains an important challenge. Conventional methods often cannot separate interfacial and bulk processes or rely on destructive analysis. Here, we demonstrate multiwavelength excitation photoluminescence (PL) as a nondestructive approach to distinguish interface- and bulk-dominated recombination losses. Using phenethylammonium tetrafluoroborate (PEABF4) treatment as a model, we use PL to show that PEABF4 passivates the electron transport layer (ETL)/perovskite interface, reducing interfacial recombination losses from fullerene deposition. However, upon thermal aging, PEABF4-treated stacks degrade more rapidly, with recombination losses broadening from the ETL/perovskite interface into the absorber. Diffusion-recombination simulations support interpreting excitation-wavelength-dependent PL decay signatures consistent with changes in surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime, providing a framework for depth-sensitive comparisons during aging. Collectively, these results further establish multiwavelength excitation PL as a platform for studying recombination losses during aging of perovskite films.

infographic.key_insight: PEABF4 treatment reduces initial recombination at the electron transport layer/perovskite interface, but treated stacks degrade faster during thermal aging as losses extend into the absorber.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Depth-sensitive photoluminescence can help engineers assess whether interface passivation improves both initial performance and thermal durability.
method: Use multiwavelength excitation photoluminescence to distinguish interface- and bulk-dominated recombination.
Track recombination changes in PEABF4-treated perovskite stacks during thermal aging.
Interpret wavelength-dependent PL decays with diffusion-recombination simulations.
infographic.evidence_signal: PL measurements indicate reduced initial losses from fullerene deposition but faster degradation after PEABF4 treatment, with simulations supporting changes in surface recombination velocity and bulk lifetime.
infographic.watch_item: Depth assignments are model-supported interpretations, and the abstract does not establish quantitative device-lifetime gains or generality beyond the studied stacks.
infographic.paper_title: Wavelength-Dependent Photoluminescence Mapping of Depth-Dependent Degradation Under Thermal Stress in Phenethylammonium Tetrafluoroborate Treated Perovskite Solar Cells

title: Readiness-Constrained Pre-Islanding Dispatch for Military Microgrids
authors: Aidan Looney, Annie Weathers, Nicholas Judson
abstract: Military installation energy readiness depends on having sufficient resources to sustain mission-critical loads throughout a prolonged utility outage. This paper develops a method to help operators manage energy resources during normal grid-connected operation while preserving islanded readiness. A robust viability kernel identifies combinations of battery energy, fuel, and load-shifting capability sufficient to sustain critical load under uncertain demand and photovoltaic generation. A probability bound translates stochastic generator start failures and recovery into a deterministic generator count selected to meet a specified availability requirement at islanding. Case studies for a fourteen-day islanding requirement at 0.999 islanding-entry availability show that advance warning of an outage can be used to prepare resources to meet a higher readiness requirement before islanding begins. The case studies further demonstrate that economic-only operation and the evaluated fixed battery reserve policy can fail to sustain critical load for the required duration, whereas enforcing the resource-dependent requirement preserves readiness at a modest increase in modeled grid-connected operating cost. These results demonstrate how active resource management can preserve long-duration energy readiness. The framework also helps commanders understand how readiness changes with operating conditions, even when the available resources remain the same.

infographic.key_insight: Resource-dependent dispatch constraints can preserve military microgrid readiness for prolonged outages while allowing economical grid-connected operation.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Coordinating battery energy, generator fuel, and load shifting helps operators sustain mission-critical loads despite uncertain demand, solar generation, and generator availability.
method: Compute a robust viability kernel defining resource combinations sufficient to sustain critical loads.
Translate generator start failures and recovery into a deterministic generator count using an availability probability bound.
Constrain pre-islanding dispatch to maintain readiness and use advance outage warning to prepare resources.
infographic.evidence_signal: Case studies targeting 14-day islanding and 0.999 islanding-entry availability found that resource-dependent constraints preserved readiness at a modest modeled cost increase, while economic-only dispatch and the evaluated fixed battery reserve policy could fail.
infographic.watch_item: Readiness guarantees depend on the assumed uncertainty bounds and generator failure-and-recovery model; the abstract reports case studies rather than field validation.
infographic.paper_title: Readiness-Constrained Pre-Islanding Dispatch for Military Microgrids

title: Which wind and solar modelling choices matter? Effects on capacity factors, energy droughts and European power system configuration
authors: L. Karkossa, A. Grochowicz, M. J. Koivisto, A. Hahmann, M. VIctoria
abstract: Europe's future power system will rely heavily on wind and solar power and must remain resilient during prolonged periods of low wind and solar generation, known as variable renewable energy (VRE) droughts. To capture such rare events, adequacy assessments increasingly draw on decades of weather data, but the conversion of weather into power is largely treated as fixed. It remains unclear which modelling choices in this conversion matter for representing these droughts, and whether they matter as much as the weather itself. Here we systematically compare these choices side by side (bias correction, wind speed extrapolation, capacity layouts, turbine and photovoltaic configurations, and wake losses) and trace their effects through VRE droughts to the design of a net-zero European power system, using 85 years of reanalysis data. We find that modelling choices barely change how often VRE droughts occur or when the system is stressed. They do, however, determine how much capacity is needed to withstand that stress. By altering the electricity delivered during droughts, they shift required capacity by up to 480 GW, which is comparable to the spread across the most critical weather years. Modelling exercises should therefore use multiple weather years; bias-correct and regionally validate weather inputs; explicitly represent resource heterogeneity, forward-looking technologies, and wake losses; and judge these choices by their effect on the low-generation tail, not only on the mean.

infographic.key_insight: Wind and solar modelling choices barely change drought frequency or stress timing, but can shift the capacity needed to withstand those droughts by up to 480 GW.
infographic.engineering_relevance: Resilient net-zero European power system planning requires testing weather-to-power assumptions, not just selecting representative weather years.
method: Compare bias correction, wind speed extrapolation, capacity layouts, turbine and photovoltaic configurations, and wake losses.
Trace their effects on renewable energy droughts and net-zero European power system design.
Evaluate low-generation periods alongside average output.
infographic.evidence_signal: Using 85 years of reanalysis data, the study finds modelling-driven capacity shifts comparable to the spread across the most critical weather years.
infographic.watch_item: Weather-to-power inputs need regional validation; matching mean generation alone may not capture performance during droughts.
infographic.paper_title: Which wind and solar modelling choices matter? Effects on capacity factors, energy droughts and European power system configuration
